excerpt: Thatch helps US employers give staff a tax-free health budget (ICHRA) to buy their own insurance. Pricing from $230 a month, funding and alternatives.
content:
Thatch is a US health benefits platform built around ICHRAs (individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements), which are now also called CHOICE arrangements. Instead of buying one group insurance plan for everyone, an employer gives each employee a tax-free monthly health budget. Employees use Thatch's marketplace to pick an individual insurance plan that suits them, and a Thatch card lets them spend any money left over on other medical costs. Thatch handles the administration, payroll integration, premium payments and compliance paperwork. It describes itself as a financial technology company; its insurance services are provided by Thatch Health Insurance Services LLC.

TechCrunch reported that Thatch was founded in October 2021 in San Francisco by Chris Ellis, its chief executive, and Adam Stevenson, its president. It raised a $38 million Series A led by General Catalyst, then a $40 million Series B in April 2025 led by Index Ventures, with a16z, General Catalyst, SemperVirens, PeopleTech Partners, The General Partnership and ADP Ventures. At that point it had 72 employees, had onboarded more than 1,000 companies in 18 months, and named customers including Dave's Hot Chicken and Jersey Mike's. QuickBooks embeds its ICHRA product.

On 16 September 2026 the law firm Latham & Watkins announced that it had advised Thatch on a $108 million Series C at a $1 billion post-money valuation, with investors including The General Partnership, Index Ventures, Scale Venture Partners, General Catalyst and Andreessen Horowitz.

Thatch publishes its prices. The Standard plan, for employers with 1 to 49 eligible employees, is $230 a month; the page's example for four employees is $45 per employee plus a $50 compliance fee. Larger employers get custom pricing with a 10-enrolled-employee minimum of $2,400 a year. It is a US-only service.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

use_cases: Offering health benefits through an ICHRA instead of a group plan
Giving employees a monthly tax-free health budget
Letting staff choose their own individual insurance plan
Automating premium payments and compliance paperwork

fit: are a US employer, especially a small or multi-state one, that finds group plans expensive or rigid
want employees to pick their own coverage
run payroll on a platform Thatch integrates with, such as QuickBooks or ADP
not_fit: want a traditional group plan with one network for everyone

notes: Insurance premiums themselves are paid from the employer's health budget and are separate from Thatch's fee.

cons: Individual-market plan choice and prices vary a lot by state

alternatives.intro: Other products that do a similar job. We have not compared them hands-on; check each one's own site for current prices.

items.difference: Covers QSEHRA, ICHRA and other HRAs.
